application_guidance.input_pattern: An exact execution of the stated constant-step FISTA on a finite-valued convex composite objective with a known valid global gradient Lipschitz constant.
read_original_when: Extending to constraints, extended-valued g, Hilbert spaces, inexact steps, stochastic gradients or backtracking.
Using any source Proof detail beyond this source-linked map.
Checking the printed p.196 squared-norm convention.
sensitive_conditions: Both f and g are convex; g is finite-valued and continuous on all R^n in this extracted statement.
The proximal operation is exact and must be accounted for separately.
The minimizer set is nonempty; the numerator depends on the chosen x* and x_0.
The guarantee applies to x_k; it does not impose a sparsity/support restriction or certify convergence of all iterates.

complexity_scope.guarantee: Deterministic inequality for every k≥1 and every minimizer x*.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: Explicit constant 2; dependence on L and ||x_0−x*||² is displayed. No unspecified asymptotic constants are needed.
complexity_scope.oracle: Exact ∇f and exact proximal operation for g/L.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Last proximal iterate x_k; objective gap F(x_k)−min F.
complexity_scope.regime: Finite-dimensional unconstrained convex composite problems under the complete statement assumptions; constant-step case only.
complexity_scope.resource: k exact gradient evaluations and k exact proximal operations, charged separately; scalar/vector arithmetic and acquisition of L are additional resources. No bound on proximal implementation work is asserted.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Selected deterministic exact constant-step FISTA only; no lower-bound coverage of an algorithm class.

issues.description: Printed p.196 later prints b_1=||u_1||²=||x_1−x*|| without the final square, whereas its b_k definition and subsequent initial-potential calculation use squared norms. The local argument uses the squared-norm convention; it is distinct from a source quotation.

evidence.statement_check: Checked Section 2.2 assumptions against PDF p.7 image, the constant-step algorithm against p.11 image, and Theorem 4.4 across pp.13–14 images; theorem is specialized to alpha=1.

content.intended_use: Supply a deterministic function-value upper bound for the specified algorithm.

proofs.locator: Lemma 2.3, printed p.190; Lemma 4.1 and Proof, printed pp.194–195; Lemmas 4.2–4.3, printed p.195; Theorem 4.4 Proof, printed p.196
map: Printed pp.189–190: Lemma 2.1 supplies majorization for the fixed L; exact subgradient optimality in Lemma 2.2 and convexity yield Lemma 2.3's basic inequality. Its Proof was read.

Printed pp.194–195: write v_k=F(x_k)−F*, u_k=t_kx_k−(t_k−1)x_{k−1}−x*. Apply Lemma 2.3 at y_{k+1} using x=x_k and x=x*. Multiply the first inequality by t_{k+1}−1, add the second, then multiply by t_{k+1}.
Use t_{k+1}²−t_{k+1}=t_k² and the displayed squared-norm identity. Substituting the y recurrence yields Lemma 4.1. For constant steps L_k=L this is E_{k+1}≤E_k for E_k=(2/L)t_k²v_k+||u_k||².
Printed p.196: apply Lemma 2.3 at y_1=x_0 and x=x*, and use t_1=1 and u_1=x_1−x*. The displayed calculation gives (2/L)v_1≤||x_0−x*||²−||x_1−x*||², hence E_1≤||x_0−x*||².
Theorem 4.4 invokes Lemma 4.2 for the potential bound and Lemma 4.3, t_k≥(k+1)/2, to conclude v_k≤2L||x_0−x*||²/(k+1)². In this constant-step specialization no backtracking bound is required.
proofs.omitted_details: Source-linked Proof map, not a new local Theorem or independent reproof. Lemmas 4.2 and 4.3 are stated without Proof in the source. Standard smoothness majorization and subgradient optimality are cited/briefly justified there. Their precise locators are retained; no separate scientific IDs are invented.
proofs.reading_coverage: Actually viewed PDF pp.7–8 and 11–14. Read basic definitions and Lemma 2.3 Proof, constant-step algorithm, entire Lemma 4.1 Proof and Theorem 4.4 Proof, plus Lemmas 4.2–4.3 statements. No whole-paper or independent Reviewer coverage is claimed.

assumptions: g:R^n→R is continuous convex, possibly nonsmooth.
f:R^n→R is convex and continuously differentiable, and ||∇f(x)−∇f(y)||≤L||x−y|| for every x,y in R^n.
The fixed positive constant L is supplied and every gradient and proximal step is exact.
statement.conclusion: 0≤F(x_k)−F(x*)≤2L||x_0−x*||²/(k+1)². This is (4.4) with alpha=1 and L=L(f), the supplied Lipschitz constant.
statement.objects_and_definitions: On R^n with Euclidean norm, F=f+g and X*=argmin F. For y in R^n define p_L(y)=argmin_x {g(x)+(L/2)||x−(y−∇f(y)/L)||²}. Set y_1=x_0,t_1=1. For k≥1 let x_k=p_L(y_k), t_{k+1}=(1+sqrt(1+4t_k²))/2, and y_{k+1}=x_k+((t_k−1)/t_{k+1})(x_k−x_{k−1}).
statement.parameter_domains: n∈{1,2,…}, L∈(0,∞), k∈{1,2,…}, x_0∈R^n; no strong convexity assumption.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every such problem, every x_0 in R^n, every supplied valid positive gradient Lipschitz constant L, every integer k≥1 and every x* in X*, the conclusion holds deterministically.
